title: Sensitivity labels: what they classify, protect and tell Copilot to leave alone
summary: The page overlooks a documented sensitivity-label setting that restricts Copilot in Office apps without requiring encryption or a DLP policy. It also implies that site labels encrypt sites and incorrectly generalizes simulation-on-save to every auto-labeling policy. Most of the configuration paths, commands and licensing statements are supported.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels classify and protect organizational data.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection let you classify and protect your organization's data

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Labels are stored in file and email metadata and stay with the content wherever it is saved.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, the label stays with the content, no matter where you save or store it.

claims.where: summary
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can encrypt the files, emails and sites named in the summary.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.
claims.fix: Replace the first summary sentence with: 'Sensitivity labels are Microsoft Purview classifications that can encrypt files and emails and control privacy and sharing for sites.' Site labels protect the container, not its individual items, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Copilot agents recognize sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and Copilot agents recognize and use the sensitivity labels that you apply to protect your organization's data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels

claims.quote: in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat conversations that can reference data from different types of items, users see the sensitivity label with the highest priority

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels; Why it matters
claims.claim: For label-encrypted items, Copilot and agents return data only when the user has EXTRACT, the permission to copy.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents return data from an item only if the user is granted permissions to copy (the EXTRACT usage right) from that item.
claims.fix: Retain the general EXTRACT rule but add: 'Microsoft documents an exception for Copilot in Edge and Windows: without DLP in Edge, it can reference encrypted content in the active Edge tab even without EXTRACT.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations#information-protection-considerations-for-microsoft-365-copilot, whose app-specific exceptions qualify the overview.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot in Word, PowerPoint and Outlook inherits the source file's label when creating new content from it.
claims.quote: the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.
claims.fix: Add: 'Label inheritance is not supported when the source is encrypted with user-defined permissions; in that case, the user cannot send the data to the destination item.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations#information-protection-considerations-for-microsoft-365-copilot. Add that URL to sources together with the Office-apps URL specified in the Open questions correction.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: Deleting a sensitivity label does not remove it from content.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label from the Microsoft Purview portal, the label isn't automatically removed from content
claims.fix: Acknowledge the cited pages' disagreement instead of giving a universal rule. Replace the first two sentences of this bullet with: 'The labels overview says deletion does not automatically remove labels or protection from content. The detailed deletion guide says container labels are removed and their settings stop being enforced; it also documents encryption removal for processable documents in enabled SharePoint and OneDrive services.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels#removing-and-deleting-labels.

claims.fix: Apply the shared deletion-bullet replacement: 'The labels overview says deletion does not automatically remove labels or protection from content. The detailed deletion guide says container labels are removed and their settings stop being enforced; it also documents encryption removal for processable documents in enabled SharePoint and OneDrive services.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels#removing-and-deleting-labels.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An encrypting default label breaks external sharing

claims.quote: It's usually not a good idea to select a label that applies encryption as a default label to documents. For example, many organizations need to send and share documents with external users who might not have apps that support the encryption or they might not use an account that can be authorized.
